body:
Global crypto markets absorbed a meaningful selloff on October 24, 2026, with total market capitalization dropping to $2.69T, a decline of -4.93% over the past 24 hours on aggregate volume of $61.5B. The mood is cautious but not panicked — the Fear & Greed index sits at 51 today versus 50 yesterday, a near-perfect Neutral reading that suggests the market is digesting losses rather than fleeing in disarray. BTC dominance climbed to 60.1%, with ETH dominance at 10.7%, the classic pattern of capital rotating defensively into bitcoin as altcoins absorb disproportionate damage. The session has the texture of a controlled flush rather than a structural breakdown, but the breadth of red across the board warrants close attention.

Bitcoin is trading at $80,539, down -1.38% over the past 24 hours and -1.16% over the past 7 days, with 24-hour volume of $22.24B. A CoinDesk live update noted bitcoin holding above $81,000 at the time of writing, suggesting the $80,539 print reflects intraday softness rather than a clean break of that psychological handle — traders will be watching whether $80,000 holds as support into the weekend. The hourly change of just +0.02% signals stabilization in the near term, but the weekly trend is still negative and the $82,000-$83,000 zone above now constitutes near-term resistance. A sustained close back above $81,500 would meaningfully improve the short-term technical picture; a break below $79,500 reopens downside toward the $77,000-$78,000 range that served as a consolidation base in prior weeks.

Ethereum is at $2,363.64, down -1.61% in 24 hours and -2.76% on the week, with volume of $8.08B — underperforming bitcoin on both timeframes and flagging continued relative weakness in the ETH/BTC ratio. The real damage, however, is concentrated in the smaller-cap layer. DOT is the session's worst performer among ZIMR tracked majors, crashing -10.06% in 24 hours to $1.06 and extending a -7.56% weekly decline, with volume a thin $0.15B that amplifies the move. UNI fell -5.37% to $6.82 and is down -6.27% on the week. LINK dropped -4.22% to $11.59, extending a -5.14% weekly slide. ADA lost -4.08% to $0.2079, now off -6.53% for the week. AVAX at $8.91 is the most stressed on the weekly basis among liquid majors, down -10.88% over 7 days despite a modest hourly bounce of +0.60%. SOL fell -3.02% to $101.29, a psychologically significant breach of the $100 handle that bears watching. The one standout on a relative basis is BNB, down only -2.00% in 24 hours to $731.22 but up +1.55% on the week — the clearest expression of Binance ecosystem resilience in an otherwise indiscriminate selloff.

The macro backdrop is adding friction at every level. Oil prices hitting a six-month high, as noted in CoinDesk's live coverage, is complicating the rates narrative by keeping inflation risk elevated and reducing the probability of near-term central bank easing — a headwind for risk assets broadly. On the regulatory front, the SEC has flagged tokenization as a high-risk area in its 2027 market examinations, which is a notable signal that institutional tokenization projects will face heightened scrutiny just as they are gaining traction. Wells Fargo and 5 other institutions have reportedly objected to OKX and ICE's tokenized stock listing plans, adding friction to one of the sector's most anticipated product rollouts. Separately, a US senator is probing Tether following a reported deal with a former Trump crypto adviser, reintroducing stablecoin counterparty risk as a headline concern. On the more constructive side, Franklin Templeton added $150 million in fund shares to the XRP Ledger in a single wallet, a concrete institutional commitment that partially explains XRP's intraday hourly bounce of +0.31% even as it remains down -3.29% on the day. The IRS signaling lower tax disclosure penalties including for crypto, per a Forbes-cited Cointelegraph report, is a quiet but positive structural development for retail participation.

Looking ahead, the immediate test is whether bitcoin can reclaim and hold $81,000 going into the weekend, when liquidity typically thins and moves can exaggerate. A failure there opens the door to a retest of the $78,000-$79,000 zone that would likely drag altcoins to fresh cycle lows — DOT and AVAX in particular have little obvious technical support below current levels. The Initia blockchain exploit draining over $2.6M, per Cointelegraph, is a reminder that security incidents can crystallize broader sentiment shifts at moments of fragility; watch for contagion risk if additional DeFi incidents emerge. The Bitcoin Core security rule update in response to AI-assisted code vulnerability discovery is worth monitoring for narrative impact — any suggestion of protocol-level risk, even if technically manageable, can move markets. On the upside, the Franklin Templeton XRP Ledger move and Robinhood's surge in bitcoin and gold prediction markets point to genuine demand formation at the retail and institutional margins. What would change the picture bullishly: a clean daily close above $83,000 in BTC, a stabilization in DOT and AVAX, and any regulatory clarity on tokenized equities. What would change it bearishly: a break below $79,000, another major exploit, or an oil-driven inflation print that pushes rate cut expectations further out.
